questions.question: Sintayehu struggles with procrastination; he wishes he ______ better time management skills to meet his assignment deadlines.
questions.explanation: When expressing a desire for a present situation to be different, 'wish' takes the Simple Past tense verb form ('had').

questions.question: Students must learn to avoid procrastination in order to submit their projects on time. What is the closest contextual meaning of 'procrastination'?

options.text: The habit of delaying or postponing tasks that require attention
The practice of waking up early in the morning
The ability to complete multiple tasks simultaneously
The act of organizing study schedules in advance

questions.explanation: In Unit 2 reading vocabulary, 'procrastination' refers to intentionally delaying or postponing tasks that need to be done.

questions.question: The student was ______ overwhelmed by his homework load that he decided to create a daily study schedule.
questions.explanation: The structure 'so + adjective + that clause' ('so overwhelmed that') is used to express cause and result.

questions.question: Whenever you encounter a difficult problem in your assignment, you should never give up; instead, ______ trying until you find the solution.
questions.explanation: The phrasal verb 'go on' means to continue doing an action without stopping.

questions.question: In English phonetics, the plural noun ending '-s' is pronounced as the distinct syllable /-iz/ after sibilant sounds. In which word is '-s' pronounced as /-iz/?
questions.explanation: Nouns ending in sibilant sounds (/s/, /z/, /ʃ/, /tʃ/, /dʒ/) add the plural suffix pronunciation /-iz/ (e.g., 'buses' /ˈbʌsɪz/).

questions.question: ______ prioritized daily schedules enables high school students to balance academic study with extracurricular activities.
questions.explanation: A gerund ('Creating') can function as the grammatical subject of a sentence.

questions.question: According to the reading text 'Cultural Views of Time Management', which cultural time view considers time as a linear, structured continuum where tasks are planned sequentially 'one at a time'?
questions.explanation: Section 2C.2 specifies that a 'linear time view' treats time as a sequential continuum where tasks are planned and executed one after another.

questions.question: It was ______ an urgent assignment that the entire research team stayed in the university library past midnight.
questions.explanation: The structure 'such + (article) + adjective + noun + that' ('such an urgent assignment that') introduces a clause of result.

questions.question: Identify the sentence structure error in the following construction: 'Chaltu follows a strict study timetable she always completes her assignments before the deadline.'

options.text: Run-on Sentence (two independent clauses joined without punctuation)
Sentence Fragment (a dependent clause standing alone)
Comma Splice (two independent clauses joined improperly with only a comma)

questions.explanation: A run-on sentence occurs when two complete independent clauses are joined together without any punctuation or coordinating conjunction between them.

questions.question: Solve the verbal analogy: 'PLENTY is to AMPLE as SHORTAGE is to ______'.
questions.explanation: In Section 2D analogies, 'plenty' and 'ample' are synonyms. Similarly, 'shortage' and 'scarcity' are synonyms.

questions.question: I am really looking forward ______ my classmates at the annual high school graduation ceremony next week.
questions.explanation: The three-word phrasal verb 'look forward to' requires a gerund/noun object following the preposition 'to' ('looking forward to seeing').

questions.question: Yared failed his final English examination because he spent all week playing video games. Now he wishes he ______ harder for the test.
questions.explanation: Expressing a past regret about an unfulfilled past action requires 'wish + Past Perfect' ('had studied').

questions.question: Which option correctly revises the run-on sentence: 'School in Munich was too rigid and boring for young Einstein he did not do well.'

options.text: School in Munich was too rigid and boring for young Einstein; consequently, he did not do well.
School in Munich was too rigid and boring for young Einstein, he did not do well.
School in Munich was too rigid and boring for young Einstein so he did not do well.
School in Munich was too rigid and boring for young Einstein, that he did not do well.

questions.explanation: Connecting two independent main clauses using a semicolon and conjunctive adverb ('; consequently,') eliminates a run-on sentence error.

questions.question: In contrast to linear time cultures, how do 'multi-active' (polychronic) cultures view time management during business meetings according to Section 2C.2?

options.text: They prioritize building relationships and maintaining high-quality social interactions over strictly adhering to meeting durations or clocks.
They strictly enforce minute-by-minute agendas and end meetings immediately when the timer expires.
They view time as a revolving circle where past and future repeat identically.
They reject all forms of face-to-face communication in favor of automated digital scheduling.

questions.explanation: Section 2C.2 explains that multi-active (polychronic) cultures focus on relationship synergy and conversation quality rather than rigid clock efficiency.

questions.question: Analyze the grammatical function of the gerund 'eating' in the sentence: 'Her favorite morning habit is eating fresh fruits before studying.'

options.text: Direct object of a transitive verb

questions.explanation: In this sentence, 'eating fresh fruits...' follows the linking verb 'is' and completes/describes the subject 'Her favorite morning habit', functioning as a subject complement.
